title: One graphic per repo, drawn
subject: The Repos lens card in the Activity view's Sessions pane

brief.background: The Repos lens drew each repo's sessions as a grid of small hub-and-spoke stars, which said little at a glance. A card should instead carry one graphic per repo that shows which repos it is worked alongside and how heavily, using size and shape, so a reader can name its usual company in one look.
brief.methodology: The eight concepts were sketched before any was judged, each from web-tools's real figures: 81 sessions, of which web-tools-private shares 69, home 52, chat-histories 16 and budget-drs 15, with 9 sessions in web-tools alone.

ideas.title: Route map
ideas.commentary: An airline's map from one hub: **web-tools** in the middle, a spoke to each repo it shared a session with, the spoke's thickness and the satellite's size both the sessions shared. It is the hub-and-spoke shape drawn once per repo instead of once per session, and it reads at a glance which ties are heavy. Even spacing says nothing, so position is spent.

ideas.title: Orbit
ideas.commentary: Closeness as gravity: each repo sits nearer the center the larger the share of **web-tools**'s sessions it was in, so web-tools-private (69 of 81) hugs the hub and the one-session repos drift to the rim. Rings at 25, 50 and 75 percent make the distance readable, and ranking the repos clockwise from twelve turns the field into a spiral.

ideas.title: Share donut
ideas.commentary: A ring around the hub, one arc per companion, its length that repo's share of all the pairings. It answers who takes most of the hub's company as a part of a whole, but the arcs sum pairings rather than sessions, since one session can pair three ways, and that total has no plain meaning.

ideas.title: Overlapping circles
ideas.commentary: Euler circles sized by each repo's own sessions, overlapping the hub's by the sessions they shared. It shows what no other concept does: **chat-histories** sits wholly inside web-tools (16 of its 16), while **home** is bigger and only partly overlaps (52 of 122). Past four or five circles the layout cannot keep every overlap true.

ideas.title: Session matrix
ideas.commentary: An event matrix: the hub's sessions as columns in time order, a row per companion, a dot where a session worked in both. It adds **when**: budget-drs joins only in November. It is a grid of dots rather than a shape, and on a phone the 81 columns are about 4 px apart.

ideas.title: Usual company
ideas.commentary: The hub's sessions grouped by the exact set of repos they worked in: with web-tools-private (p) and home (h) 19, with web-tools-private alone 14, alone 9. It reads the recurring teams rather than pairs, which the other concepts flatten, but the long tail of one-off sets crowds the bottom.

grafts: spokes whose thickness is the sessions shared, so the heavy ties read before the distances do
a ring around each companion filled to the share of its own sessions spent with the hub, so chat-histories (16 of 16) and home (52 of 122) differ
the sessions the hub had alone, stated at its center
a table under the graphic with the exact figures for each companion
selection.rationale: The orbit spends both of a radial graphic's channels: distance carries how much of the hub's work a repo is part of, and the ranked spiral keeps the strongest ties together at the top. The spokes keep the hub-and-spoke shape the owner found interesting, and the ring adds the reverse direction, how much of the companion's own life runs through the hub, which only the Euler circles otherwise show. The same rules draw the All repos card, with every session as the hub.
assumptions: Is the share of the hub's sessions the right closeness, or should lines changed count, since session-record writes may inflate web-tools-private?
Does a reader take the ring around a companion as its own share without a legend?
Does ranking clockwise read as order, or does position look arbitrary?
Is 'when' (concepts 6 and 8) the next thing a repo's card should show?
